extracted.intended_audience: reading researchers, linguists, journalism educators, and journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative and prescriptive criteria for writing and analyzing newspaper news stories with emphasis on discourse-level organization, connectives, and readability for comprehension. Targets improvements in newswriting pedagogy and text design to enhance reader comprehension without sacrificing journalistic objectivity or timeliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical organization and explicit connectives as primary determinants
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical organization and explicit connectives should be the most important determinants of the story's form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author argues editors should insist that logical organization and explicit connectives be emphasized over other concerns; examples of desirable connectives given (accordingly, finally, thus, so, as a consequence). Claims increased explicit connection will make stories more, not less, skimmable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize clarity over sentence length, 'human interest', and editors' convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence length, 'human interest,' and the editor's convenience should be considered of less importance than logical organization and clarity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate sentences by asking not 'Are they short enough?' but 'Is it going to be clear to the reader what the relevance of this information is, what the point of including it is?'; warns against valuing flashiness ('Is it flashy...vivid enough?') instead of structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotes and colorful details only when they serve the news point
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes and colorful details that are included merely to 'brighten up' a story are likely to attract attention away from the news point and reduce the story to a jumbled collection of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should discourage adding anecdotal or decorative material for its own sake; such material should be included only when it directly supports the story's point or logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the story's point and relevance explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: The important question to ask about a story should be 'Is this a logically structured account?' rather than whether it is flashy; the relevance of each piece of information should be clear to the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for writers: explicitly signal why information is included and how it contributes to the story's point; avoid leaving the 'why' implicit and forcing readers to infer connections from adjacency alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit causal/logical connectives where warranted
rubrics_metrics.description: Use connective words (e.g., accordingly, finally, thus, so, as a consequence) to make causal and logical relationships explicit rather than relying on 'and' or merely temporal connectives that only implicate causation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text contrasts recommended connectives with the common practice of using 'and' or 'when/after' to imply causality; cites AP examples where omission of causal connectives burdens the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid omitting connectives that create comprehension demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Omission of causal connectives can leave readers without appreciation of the demands this omission makes on comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides examples where reporters omit causal markers and editors/teachers praise superficial touches rather than explaining causal links; recommends adding explicit connectives to relieve reader inference burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for producer intentions and pragmatics in discourse structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Text structure at the discourse level is significantly affected by the perceived goals of the producer; text-linguists and writers must take into account the producer's presumable intentions in producing the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implication for analysis and instruction: incorporate pragmatics (producer goals) when describing or teaching text organization; understand that newsroom practices and institutional goals shape organizational choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve objectivity and timeliness while increasing explicit organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Making newswriting more like other expository genres should not sacrifice the objectivity and timeliness that are proper goals of newswriting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipates reporter objections that connectives constitute interpretation; argues that appropriate use of logical connectives can clarify without improperly interpreting facts and that objectivity concerns should not be used to avoid clear organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use paragraphing and connected discourse instead of isolated short sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of paragraphing and excessive use of very short sentences lead to inexplicit connections among ideas; connected discourse with paragraphing aids comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares primers and newswriting, noting primers often eliminate connectives and paragraphing; suggests that placing related sentences into connected paragraphs highlights structure and eases inference for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach reporters to highlight and enhance natural story structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction should concentrate on highlighting and enhancing whatever natural structure inheres in a story, not on teaching reporters cheap tricks to hide a multitude of flaws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical recommendation: training should focus on revealing inherent organizational relations (order, connectives) rather than surface 'brightening' tactics that distract from the point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'fog' and unnecessary complexity in news prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing full of fog and unnecessary complexity impedes readership and comprehension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites earlier critics (Gunning) and argues that much reading difficulty is caused by poor writing; recommends simplification and clarity rather than opaque style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use headings or category labels to improve comprehensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely adding a title or category label to a text can significantly improve comprehensibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Bransford and Johnson (1973) demonstration that a title improves understanding; suggests similar small explicit labels can make otherwise disconnected news text easier to comprehend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow natural sentence length and connective use in early schooling materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Loosening sentence length requirements (after mid-first-grade competence) to allow more natural use of connectives may not delay decoding and might hasten comprehension-skill development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes experiments to test whether permitting longer, more connected sentences in early reading instruction affects acquisition of decoding and sentence-comprehension skills; pedagogical implication for texts used in reading instruction.
